newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-NO BLOCKBUSTER DEALS AS TRADE DEADLINE PASSES.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-NO BLOCKBUSTER DEALS AS TRADE DEADLINE PASSES.

text.p: There was a flurry of trading activity around the National Basketball Association on Thursday but no major stars changed teams as the 1996-97 trading deadline passed.
Mark Jackson, the NBA's assist leader this season, was the biggest name involved in deals completed prior to the 6 p.m. (2200 GMT) deadline for teams to make trades.
A pair of All-Stars at the centre of trade rumours -- Sacramento Kings guard Mitch Richmond and Golden State Warriors small forward Chris Mullin remained with their teams.

But Jackson is back with the Pacers after new Denver Nuggets general manager Allan Bristow sent the 10-year veteran guard, rookie forward Darvin Ham and centre LaSalle Thompson to Indiana in exchange for swingman Vincent Askew, guard Jerome Allen, forward Eddie Johnson and second-round draft picks in 1997 and 1998..

Indiana had traded Jackson to Denver last summer but apparently decided they were in need of his play-making abilities. Jackson was averaging an NBA-best 12.3 assists along with 10.4 points and 5.2 rebounds in 52 games for the Nuggets this season.
The New Jersey Nets shipped one of the players they acquired earlier this week in a nine-player deal with the Dallas Mavericks to Los Angeles before he had played a single game for New Jersey.
The Los Angeles Lakers picked up swingman George McCloud from the Nets in exchange for reserve centre Joe Kleine, a first round pick in 1997 and a conditional second round pick.
McCloud is a long-range shooter who averaged 13.7 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.27 steals in 41 games for the Mavericks.

The McCloud trade had to wait until Monday's nine-player Dallas-New Jersey deal became official. That happened earlier Thursday after guard Khalid Reeves passed a physical examination for the Mavericks.
Dallas had held up the deal pending the result of stress tests on Reeves after finding out he had a heart murmur as a child, a condition that was not known to them at the time of the trade.
The Charlotte Hornets made a pair of deals Thursday.
Charlotte bolstered its backcourt by acquiring veteran shooting guard Ricky Pierce from Denver in exchange for youthful centre George Zidek and guard Anthony Goldwire.
The 37-year-old Pierce is averaging 10.2 points in 33 games for Denver this season. Goldwire, 25, averaged 5.8 points and 2.9 assists. Zidek, 23, was a member of UCLA's 1995 NCAA Championship team.
The Hornets also sent often-injured forward Scott Burrell to the Golden State Warriors for journeyman reserve forward Donald Royal, who joins his third team this season.
In another less than earth shattering deal, the Toronto Raptors acquired guard Shawn Respert from the Milwaukee Bucks for centre Acie Earl.
